judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly diagnoses stale discovery and supplies the required restart-plus-listing recovery with the exact `maui-data-binding` capability. A is tentative, diverts to unnecessary verification, and leaves the needed workflow uncertain.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and accurately fulfills the requested capability selection and Copilot CLI setup without implementation. A misses the marketplace specialist and gives misleading, non-actionable integration advice, which fails two central requirements.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Both give the same appropriate specialist and refrain from migration, but B better meets the requested marketplace-preparation workflow and is the only one to mention fixture-isolation/shared-state concerns. Its installation and post-restart discovery guidance is substantially more complete.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: A gives the precise, bounded diagnosis and smallest repair while clearly preserving the binary log's evidentiary limits. B gets the missing path right but dilutes the repair with unsupported configuration alternatives, speculative causes, and an invented placeholder file content.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are broadly relevant Python-only responses and have the same file-change violation. B is modestly stronger technically because its primary implementation preserves the original merge operation, whereas A substitutes an index join and makes a false statement about merge sorting.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the central marketplace-specialist and Codex-setup request and correctly avoids performing a migration. Its risk discussion is too terse to fully satisfy that rubric, but it is substantially more useful and complete than A's request for clarification.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Consolidate duplicate public helpers without breaking shipped callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The functional changes are equivalent and satisfy both required outcomes. Both validate the solution tests; run A also explicitly builds Fixture.sln, while B adds a documentation comment, neither creating a meaningful final-result advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a framework and package upgrade dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the required refactoring boundary exactly, refuses the behavior-affecting upgrade, confirms no changes, and routes it correctly. A performs precisely the disallowed work and mischaracterizes it as behavior-preserving.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a new-feature request dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses take the prohibited path of implementing the requested feature and labeling it behavior-preserving, rather than declining and directing the request through the feature workflow. Their rubric compliance is equivalently absent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract shared discount logic without collapsing distinct inputs
judgeRationales.rationale: The two agents reached the same correct final implementation and reported equivalent successful build/test verification; there is no final-result quality difference.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract subtotal calculation without changing arithmetic
judgeRationales.rationale: Both deliver the requested minimal behavior-preserving refactor. The only implementation difference is that A makes the private helper static while B makes it an instance method; neither affects the requested behavior or rubric compliance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Inline a pass-through wrapper and update callers
judgeRationales.rationale: Both final results satisfy the requested inline refactor with the same focused edits and successful verification; no material quality difference is evidenced.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a shipped nullable contract out of a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs satisfy the misleading requested edit rather than recognizing and preserving the shipped nullable source contract. Their final artifacts and conclusions fail both rubric criteria to the same extent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep behavior-changing bug fixes out of a behavior-preserving refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B fully follows the refactoring constraint: it safely completes and validates the rename, retains $100 behavior, and clearly defers the incompatible feature change. A makes and masks an invoice behavior change while falsely presenting it as a refactor.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Merge two near-identical types into one parameterized type
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a serialized name while renaming a C# property
judgeRationales.rationale: The evidence shows materially identical, correct implementations and validation: Tier is the C# API while LoyaltyLevel remains the JSON wire name.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a shipped wrapper while inlining ordinary callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The runs produce the same minimal, correct refactor and preserve the same compatibility test and public forwarding API. Both have passing multi-target test/build evidence; neither has a material final-result advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a helper used in every target-framework branch
judgeRationales.rationale: Both final results are substantively identical and fully satisfy the rename and label-preservation requirements, with successful solution-level multi-target validation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a member declared by a generated partial source
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents produced the same correct, minimal source changes in the required files and validated them with successful builds and all 17 tests passing for net8.0 and net10.0.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a shipped public method without breaking existing callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The final implementations are substantively equivalent and satisfy all requested compatibility, caller-migration, test, and shipped-surface requirements. Differences such as qualifying Obsolete with System do not affect result quality.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename an internal member used by a friend assembly
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents achieved the requested behavior-preserving rename and friend-assembly migration, with equivalent source-level verification and successful Fixture.sln build/test validation. Run B's initially invalid `--quiet` baseline command was recovered and does not affect the final result.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely follows the intended stale-discovery recovery sequence and addresses the requested MAUI data-binding workflow. A misdiagnoses the situation and prematurely recommends reinstall/enable actions.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely selects the relevant Blazor specialist and supplies actionable install, restart, and verification steps while respecting the no-implementation constraint. A is non-destructive but substitutes a generic/custom-agent discussion for the requested marketplace-ready specialist workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly selects the relevant named specialist and gives actionable Copilot CLI installation and discovery steps while preserving the requested no-code-change boundary. A diagnoses the issue correctly but does not provide comparably usable marketplace preparation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: B better fulfills the core preparation request through the exact specialist/plugin and complete Copilot CLI restart/discovery workflow. A gives stronger general compatibility detail, but its missing discovery step is a material usability gap.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the available marketplace route to the exact dotnet-webapi specialist and, most importantly, gives verified usable Copilot CLI installation and restart/discovery instructions. A supplies stronger technical upload guardrails but substitutes a custom agent and omits the required post-restart discovery procedure.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies every requested preparation detail and is notably stronger on installation verification and post-restart discovery. The core specialist recommendation and non-editing restraint are otherwise equivalent, so the overall quality advantage is slight.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Both reach the correct specialist and safely stop at preparation. B is the better final answer because its Copilot CLI enablement path is concrete and, critically, includes restart plus `/skills` verification, while also making the deployed-evidence versus optimization distinction more direct.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy the .NET and file-safety constraints, but A gives a safer general optimization that maintains inferred key representation and uses pandas merge directly. B's hard-coded int32 conversion is a serious correctness regression for unknown large CSV schemas, despite otherwise relevant performance suggestions. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: Neither response cleanly gives the intended concise refresh-first resolution. A is closer to the correct stale-discovery diagnosis and prioritizes restart rather than reversing the successful installation, while B supplies useful binding detail but fundamentally misdiagnoses the situation and directs an unnecessary install. A's missing post-restart listing and invented manual skill command keep the advantage modest.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and accurately fulfills all requested parts with actionable Copilot CLI marketplace steps and no component implementation. A misses the specific Copilot capability and installation workflow and unnecessarily supplies implementation code.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B fully and concisely answers the specialist and Copilot CLI setup request, including verification, while respecting the instruction not to write the utility. A largely defers the task through unnecessary clarification and omits the required setup.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly names a concrete maintained migration route and supplies actionable Copilot CLI marketplace installation, restart, and discovery instructions while preserving the project. A is largely speculative, with unverifiable specialist names and configuration/CLI syntax, despite correctly mentioning compatibility concerns.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly fulfills the preparation-only request with the precise specialist, plugin, mappings, installation commands, and discovery check, while preserving the project unchanged. A is safe in not migrating but largely defers the core marketplace request and supplies speculative guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B is modestly better overall because it bases the specialist recommendation on the csharp-expert asset actually found in the project and gives more plausible installation-oriented steps. Both are incomplete on the crucial restart/discovery requirement, and A has a somewhat stronger abstract streaming-capability description but relies on unverified Copilot CLI configuration and invocation syntax.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly fulfills the central request with a concrete maintained skill and usable Copilot CLI availability and verification steps, while A hallucinates or at least fails to substantiate the specialist and does not explain installation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Both reach the correct specialist and preserve vendor neutrality, but B directly fulfills the central operational requirement with usable marketplace installation, restart, and skill-discovery steps while remaining appropriately scoped to preparation. A lacks those required discovery steps and includes a likely unsuitable installation path plus unnecessary collection instructions.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the request with ordered, separately named capability providers and executable Copilot CLI preparation commands, while A’s generic agent labels and speculative workflow instructions fail the core availability/install requirement. Both appropriately refrain from project creation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both have the same clean .NET-related behavior and the same file-creation violation. A is modestly stronger on the substantive Python response because it offers a more complete pandas-only implementation and chunking guidance, though neither fully guarantees identical output in all edge cases (notably overlapping non-key column names and forced int32 IDs).

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the core request with the named maintained marketplace specialist and a usable Codex plugin installation path, while A is largely generic and relies on speculative commands and a made-up example package. Both incompletely discuss migration risks, but B is clearly the substantially more useful and correct result.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely diagnoses stale skill discovery and supplies the required restart, listing, and maui-data-binding verification sequence. A does not solve the reported issue and unnecessarily casts doubt on the already successful installation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly maps the two requested phases to the actual specialized skills and gives executable marketplace installation and verification instructions, while respecting the no-project-creation boundary. A has the correct high-level phase ordering but substitutes vague custom roles for the requested capability providers.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy all explicit rubric criteria equally. On response quality, A is slightly preferable because its proposed merge preserves the original left-row ordering, whereas B sorts both inputs and therefore changes the ordinary pandas inner-merge output order while claiming the result is unchanged. B also forces an int64 key, which can fail or alter valid string/nullable identifiers, and makes unsupported claims about a sorted merge path. A still has semantic edge cases from converting unmatched categorical values to missing, so the gap is modest.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs make the same correct, minimal functional refactor, preserve the shipped APIs, find no production callers requiring migration, and validate successfully. A adds a helpful XML remark, while B separately runs dotnet build in addition to tests; these are minor process/presentation differences with no material final-quality advantage.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a new-feature request dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely follows all three rubric requirements by declining the behavior-changing request and routing it appropriately. A performs the prohibited feature implementation despite passing existing tests.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract shared discount logic without collapsing distinct inputs
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are behavior-preserving validated refactors, but B has the cleaner and more accurately scoped ApplyTierDiscount helper: it extracts only the tier discount while retaining tax and final rounding in their original separate calculation paths.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract subtotal calculation without changing arithmetic
judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes are substantively identical and fully satisfy both requested refactoring and behavior-preservation requirements; both verify the solution successfully.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Inline a pass-through wrapper and update callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes satisfy both task requirements equally and are similarly focused. Run B documents a more extensive pre-change check, but that does not make its resulting refactor materially better than Run A's.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a shipped nullable contract out of a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly resisted an unsafe request after verifying the API is shipped and clearly explained why no change was appropriate. A implemented precisely the breaking public-contract change the rubric prohibits; passing build/tests does not repair that API compatibility failure.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep behavior-changing bug fixes out of a behavior-preserving refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Merge two near-identical types into one parameterized type
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs compile and pass all 17 tests on net8.0 and net10.0, but B performs the specified consolidation cleanly and migrates the actual usage. A preserves compatibility by adding a base class beneath the two original classes, which is an incomplete consolidation for an explicit single-type request.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a helper used in every target-framework branch

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a method without breaking a configured reflection name
judgeRationales.rationale: The resulting code and compatibility behavior are substantively identical and fully satisfy the requested refactor. Both validate Fixture.sln tests successfully across net8.0 and net10.0; B additionally reports an explicit build, but that does not create a meaningful final-result quality difference.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a shipped public method without breaking existing callers
judgeRationales.rationale: Both implementations satisfy the functional compatibility and test requirements, but B has cleaner warning handling and, importantly, correct shipped-versus-unshipped public API bookkeeping. A's addition of the new API to the shipped baseline is a modest release-contract/versioning error.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename an internal member used by a friend assembly
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs achieve the requested refactor completely and validate it successfully. Response B is more detailed in its report, but this does not represent a material final-result quality advantage.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses achieve the requested scoped refactor and substantiate it with successful Fixture.sln validation. B separately runs an explicit build while A's test invocation also builds the solution; this does not create a meaningful final-quality difference.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for an ordinary feature request
judgeRationales.rationale: The final implementations described and evidenced are substantively the same and fully address the single rubric criterion; neither has a material quality advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Assess a supported workload-specific build improvement
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B provides a more systematic and rigorous analysis. It explicitly enumerates all control mechanisms in a structured format, shows the mathematical calculation formally, disqualifies universal claims more forcefully, and presents the information in a well-organized table. Response A is solid and correct but somewhat less systematic and formal in its presentation. Both arrive at the correct answer with appropriate caveats, but Response B's analytical clarity and directness give it an edge, though the difference is not large enough to be considered much-better."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep SDK installation separate from build analysis
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses are of equivalent quality in addressing the task. They correctly identified that 10.0.114 is already installed and satisfies the global.json requirement (version 10.0.100 with rollForward: latestPatch), and both properly advised against installing any other SDK. Both strictly adhered to the constraint of not modifying the repo or performing any build operations. Response A is slightly more detailed in explaining why other versions shouldn't be installed, while Response B is marginally more efficient in tool usage. These minor differences do not create a meaningful quality gap."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a C sharp rename out of build authoring
judgeRationales.rationale: Response A delivers a more systematically comprehensive refactoring plan with stronger emphasis on binary compatibility and external caller considerations (API baselines, package consumers, comprehensive reference search). It provides better code examples with DiagnosticId and clearer distinctions between internal vs. public APIs. Response B excels in special-case handling (virtual methods, interfaces) and release cycle management, but falls short on the primary rubric criterion regarding external caller compatibility. Both avoid the pitfall of turning this into build system analysis. The difference is subtle but measurable in meeting the core rubric requirements."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep failing assertions out of build troubleshooting
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses appropriately address the task with strong focus on rounding behavior and decimal calculations, and both respect the constraint to avoid project/framework changes. Response A provides excellent diagnostic detail (G29 formatting for full precision inspection). Response B is slightly better overall because it provides more immediately actionable guidance: a concrete `dotnet test --filter` command to isolate and run the failing test with enhanced verbosity, and it explicitly questions the test's expected-value construction itself. While both approaches are sound, Response B's combination of conceptual explanation plus practical execution steps makes it marginally more useful for actual investigation work."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Consolidate duplicate public helpers without breaking shipped callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes are substantively identical and satisfy both rubric requirements. Both also report successful solution build/test verification.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a framework and package upgrade dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses fail every stated safety/workflow criterion in the same fundamental way: they execute and endorse major-version upgrades as behavior-preserving refactoring rather than refusing and routing to the required upgrade workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a new-feature request dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses make the same fundamental mistake required by the task's rubric: they implement and endorse a new pricing feature as a refactor rather than declining to change behavior and directing it through feature workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract shared discount logic without collapsing distinct inputs
judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes are materially identical and fully satisfy all three criteria; both trajectories demonstrate successful Fixture.sln verification and passing tests.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract subtotal calculation without changing arithmetic
judgeRationales.rationale: The resulting source changes are substantively identical and fully satisfy the requested behavior-preserving extraction. Run B additionally reports a separate build, but that does not make the final implementation meaningfully better given both solutions' successful Fixture.sln test verification.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Inline a pass-through wrapper and update callers
judgeRationales.rationale: Both final code changes satisfy the requested inline refactor equally well. Response B documents build/test validation more specifically, but this does not create a meaningful final-result quality difference given the same correct, minimal patch.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a shipped nullable contract out of a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly refuses an incompatible public API annotation change and preserves the baseline. A implements and rationalizes precisely the breaking source-contract change the rubric says to avoid.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a shipped wrapper while inlining ordinary callers
judgeRationales.rationale: Both implementations preserve behavior, migrate the ordinary caller, and keep the compatibility test. B is superior because it actually deprecates the retained shipped legacy API while keeping it callable; A leaves the old API without the required Obsolete marking.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a helper used in every target-framework branch
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents completed the requested focused refactor and supplied equivalent successful dual-framework build and test validation, with no evidenced functional or output-quality difference.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents arrived at the same correct refactor and successfully built/tested the solution. Run A briefly tried an unsuitable attribute approach but corrected it; the final delivered code and validation are equivalent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Choose LSP diagnostics before building
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses are broadly correct and comply with the stop-before-edit/build constraint. B is modestly more useful for scoping the diagnosis and connecting the List<string>-to-int mismatch to the required counting result, though A is clearer about a named diagnostics command and neither gives the exact minimal Count() repair.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a language semantic fix in the fallback
judgeRationales.rationale: Both answers are correct and directly satisfy the task. A is narrowly better because its snippet is the truly minimal ownership-only change and therefore more strictly preserves preexisting behavior; B's extra null guard is unnecessary.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: Both miss the core stale-discovery framing and prematurely recommend reinstalling. A nevertheless provides the actionable restart-then-list sequence and, crucially, the exact `maui-data-binding` capability the user needs to find; B does neither with sufficient specificity.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly fulfills the request with the exact specialist capability, actionable Copilot CLI setup, and discovery check while not implementing anything. A is generic and omits the essential CLI marketplace workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B accurately identifies the relevant installed skill, gives actionable Copilot CLI setup and verification instructions, and respects the request not to write the utility. A's central premise and setup path are unsupported and fail the requested workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: The answers are otherwise essentially equivalent and both miss the requested risk explanation, but B uniquely includes the required restart-before-discovery step while also leaving the project unchanged.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B better fulfills the central request by naming an actual specialist and giving actionable Copilot CLI installation and discovery steps. A offers useful implementation-oriented considerations and slightly more application context, but its proposed generic specialist and CLI exposure guidance are less usable.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: Both answers are accurate and fulfill the requested preparation. A is modestly stronger because it ties the recommendation to the actual N+1 order/line loading pattern and gives slightly more precise restart guidance, while still stopping before any change.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases

A preserves order and avoids scaffolding, but its generic invented specialist descriptions and non-actionable configuration guidance miss the requested marketplace preparation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Choose LSP diagnostics before building
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs fully satisfy all requested steps with accurate diagnosis, appropriately narrow repair guidance, and no prohibited edit or build. Their minor wording differences do not create a meaningful quality gap.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely follows the requested stale-discovery recovery flow and identifies the expected MAUI data-binding workflow. A incorrectly treats the issue as an unavailable capability in its own environment and does not help refresh discovery.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the requested specialist selection and provides actionable Copilot CLI preparation and verification steps while respecting the no-implementation constraint. A misses the available specialist and does not provide usable CLI installation instructions.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and concisely fulfills all requested elements with a named specialist, actionable Copilot CLI setup/discovery instructions, and no utility code. A fails the core specialist and installation requests.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: A's recommendation and installation command are directly grounded in the maintained `github/awesome-copilot` `dotnet-upgrade` skill discovered during its run. B provides more explicit post-restart wording but centers on an unsubstantiated specialist and installation route, making its core answer unreliable. A's only meaningful omission is explicit post-restart discovery guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Both correctly select the specialist and avoid changing the fixture. B is better because it directly addresses fixture isolation and, most importantly, gives a complete install, restart, and discovery path; that is a meaningful but bounded improvement over A.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B is grounded in the actual ASP.NET Core project and the exact marketplace specialist, with actionable install, restart, and discovery instructions. A gives technically sensible upload guidance but recommends a custom agent and weaker availability steps.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses fulfill the task well and accurately. B is modestly stronger because its explanation more directly and completely ties the specialist to the requested round-trip reduction while preserving the returned shape.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy the rubric cleanly, but A is modestly more precise and polished, while B makes an unsupported indexed/sorted-merge claim and leaves dead code.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: A is the more complete and operationally useful marketplace-preparation answer, particularly on the skill's scope and Codex discovery. B is better at briefly identifying an isolation/parameterized-case preservation concern, but both inadequately explain the full set of pre-migration risks.
